--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.laplacian_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Compute Laplacian centrality for each node. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.laplacian_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Compute Laplacian centrality for each node. title: >- [Graph.laplacian_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Compute Laplacian centrality for each node. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute Laplacian centrality for each node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L56377-L56519){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.laplacian_centrality( normalized=True, weighted=None, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Laplacian centrality](../assets/graphs/laplacian-centrality.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared seven-node graph shaded by Laplacian centrality, the share of the graph's Laplacian energy lost when a node is removed. Removing hub C costs the most, 0.60, then D 0.46, B and E 0.43, while the pendant node G costs only 0.09." width="100%"} Laplacian centrality measures how much the overall connectivity of the network is disrupted by removing a node. The Laplacian energy of a graph is the sum of the squared eigenvalues of its Laplacian matrix, and a node's score is the energy lost when that node is removed. With $w_{uv}$ the weight between nodes $u$ and $v$ and $s(v)$ the strength of $v$ (the sum of its edge weights), the drop has a closed form: $$\Delta E(v) = s(v)^2 + \sum_{u \in N(v)} w_{uv}^2 + 2 \sum_{u \in N(v)} s(u) w_{uv}$$ On an unweighted simple graph every $w_{uv}$ is `1` and $s(v)$ is the degree, so this is $d(v)^2 + d(v) + 2 \sum_{u \in N(v)} d(u)$. Parallel edges add their weights into one link, self-loops are ignored (they don't change the Laplacian), and on a directed graph the edge directions are ignored. When normalized (the default), the drop is divided by the Laplacian energy of the whole graph, $E = \sum_v s(v)^2 + 2 \sum_{u < v} w_{uv}^2$, so a score is the fraction of the energy lost when the node goes. The scores don't sum to `1.0`, since every edge counts toward the drop at both of its ends. On an undirected graph the results match `networkx.laplacian_centrality`; NetworkX uses a different, random-walk Laplacian for directed graphs. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (the default), divide each drop by the Laplacian energy of the graph. If `False`, return the raw energy drops. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights. If `None` (the default), uses weights when the graph is weighted. If `False`, every edge counts as `1`. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name for the node attribute to store results. If not provided, defaults to `"laplacian_centrality"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, return the raw dictionary. If `False`, store as node attributes and return self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to Laplacian centrality scores. Otherwise returns self. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If weights are used and an edge has a negative or infinite weight. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~degree_centrality`) : A simpler local measure. [](`~betweenness_centrality`) : Another view of which nodes hold the graph together. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Removing the hub of a star takes every edge with it, so it loses all of the graph's Laplacian energy and scores `1`: ::: {#8ff113ba .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec star = ec.Graph.from_edges( [("hub", "A"), ("hub", "B"), ("hub", "C"), ("hub", "D")] ) star.laplacian_centrality().get_node_df().select( "label", "laplacian_centrality" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ### Heavy ties In *Les Misérables*, each edge weight counts the chapters in which two characters appear together. Valjean tops the ranking with or without them. But with them, Cosette climbs from eighteenth to third: the ties to Valjean (31 chapters) and Marius (21) are the two heaviest in the novel. Gavroche, with many light ties, falls from second to tenth: ::: {#1828c324 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl lesmis = ( ec.les_miserables() .laplacian_centrality() .laplacian_centrality(weighted=False, attr_name="unweighted") ) ( lesmis.get_node_df() .with_columns( pl.col("laplacian_centrality", "unweighted") .rank("min", descending=True) .cast(pl.Int64) .name.suffix("_rank") ) .select( "label", "degree", "laplacian_centrality_rank", "unweighted_rank" ) .sort("laplacian_centrality_rank") .head(6) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Weights add to the energy, so they should measure the strength of a tie. A weight that measures a cost, such as the travel times in `metro()`, has the opposite meaning; pass `weighted=False` for such graphs.
